summary: New Zealand has no subsidies or contracts for difference, so independent developers need long-term PPAs, and the corporate PPA market is still young. Consenting has been made much easier since 2024, and overseas investors may need consent.

access.reason: There are no government incentive schemes, and securing offtake to raise debt is a key barrier for independent developers.

terms.reason: Spot prices are nodal and volatile, so developers seek long-term PPAs to hedge.

buyer.reason: The creditworthiness of offtakers is an important factor for developers.

ownership.reason: Overseas investors may need consent under the Overseas Investment Act 2005, and there are no foreign exchange controls.

build.reason: The Fast-track Approvals Act 2024 and 2025 resource management changes ease consents and give renewable projects a default 35-year consent.

stability.reason: National direction for renewable generation and networks was strengthened in January 2026.

direction.reason: Consenting reforms in 2024, 2025 and 2026 make new projects easier to approve.

access.reason: Physical and virtual corporate PPAs are available, but the market remains relatively nascent.

terms.reason: PPAs are flexible and can include renewable energy certificates.

ownership.reason: Overseas Investment Act consent may be needed, and there are no foreign exchange controls.

direction.reason: Corporate PPA activity is expected to increase.

events.title: Fast-track Approvals Act gives quicker consents to significant projects
Resource management amendment sets a 35-year default consent for renewables
Updated national policy statement for renewable generation and networks

sources.title: New Zealand Country Commercial Guide, trade financing

gaps: Grid connection times and curtailment were not covered by the sources reviewed.
